reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that annealing introduces L12 precipitates and increases yield strength, but it does not provide data on ductility improvement, dislocation homogenization, or pile-up reduction. The key premises about ductility enhancement and the specific mechanism are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Short-time annealing at ~700 °C for 5–10 min can induce coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates in the FCC phase of Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
These L12 precipitates will homogenize dislocation motion and reduce pile-ups at lamellar boundaries.
Reducing pile-ups will alleviate stress concentrations and suppress microcrack initiation.
The intervention will increase yield strength and significantly improve room-temperature tensile ductility (e.g., from ~8% to ~20% elongation).
